## Rescale is Now in Claude and ChatGPT


Kevin Cangemi


November 16, 2026


##### Connect Claude or ChatGPT to Rescale’s digital engineering platform to accelerate product development.


## **Expanding The engineering ecosystem**

Rescale is now available inside Claude and ChatGPT, increasing the interoperability between two of the most used AI assistants and Rescale, the leading digital engineering platform Engineers can add Rescale from the[Claude Connectors Directory](https://claude.ai/directory/connectors/mcp-services-platform-rescale-com) or the[ChatGPT plugins directory](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugin_asdk_app_6ad8ebb232388191bf7f866c50451ae3) , then sign in with their Rescale account. From there, they ask for what they need in plain language. They can start with basic questions to explore data, then move to initiating Rescale actions like kicking off jobs and invoking workflow agents. Pull up last week’s crash runs, or have it read the logs on a failed job and explain what went wrong. Hand the assistant an input deck and get back an Ansys Fluent job configured on 64 cores, ready to review before anything is submitted.


Both listings run on the Rescale MCP server, which also works with coding tools like Claude Code and Codex. The assistant works in the Rescale workspace the engineer picks at sign-in and has only that engineer’s permissions. It records every action under their name.


## **How the Rescale MCP server works**


Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard for connecting AI assistants to the systems where work happens. Claude and ChatGPT both support it, and the list of engineering tools that will “speak MCP” is likely to grow. As more simulation and engineering specific software adds MCP connections, Rescale will be able to plug in without custom integration work.


The Rescale MCP server is a hosted service that presents the Rescale platform to an assistant as tools it can call. Nothing to install. When an engineer asks a question, the assistant decides which tools it needs, runs them with that engineer’s Rescale credentials, and works the results into its answer alongside files attached to the chat or data from other connected tools.


Claude or ChatGPT can also call Rescale Edison, the platform’s AI assistant and agent orchestrator. Edison works from what’s already in your Rescale workspace, including your jobs, simulation results, and operational data, so its answers reflect your actual runs rather than general knowledge. On Advanced Modeling & Simulation, Edison can analyze that data directly. On[Rescale Agentic Engineering](https://rescale.com/solutions/agentic-digital-engineering/) , it also routes requests to specialized agents, such as Job Troubleshooter, and returns a single result grounded in your own engineering data.


## **What you can ask**


Once Rescale is connected, engineers use it in the same chat where they already do the rest of their work. Some prompts to start with:


- “Which versions of Simcenter STAR-CCM+ can I run, and on which hardware?”
- “Here’s my input deck. Set up an Ansys Fluent job on 64 cores and show me the settings before submitting.”
- “Show my recently completed Rescale jobs and summarize the latest result.”
- “Job \[JOB_ID\] failed. Read the logs and explain what went wrong.”
- “Ask Rescale to troubleshoot job \[JOB_ID\] and suggest a fix.” (Agentic Engineering)


What your AI tool can do in Rescale varies by your plan, ranging from analyzing job results, to building workflows, to calling specialized agents to build reports.


**Rescale plan** **What Claude and ChatGPT can work with**


Every Rescale plan Jobs, files, and workstations, plus the software and hardware available to you


[Advanced Modeling & Simulation](https://rescale.com/solutions/advanced-modeling-simulation/) Adds Workflow Builder workflows, which the assistant can run and track, plus Rescale Edison to analyze your simulation and operational data

## **What this means for engineering teams**


The point is fewer context switches between the assistant where engineers think and the platform where their simulations run.


- **Seamlessly integrate Rescale into multi-tool workflows.** Claude and ChatGPT can call Rescale in the same conversation as other connected tools, including MCP servers from other engineering software. One conversation can pull a spec from one system, run the simulation on Rescale, and draft the report somewhere else.
- **Job setup starts from the files you already have.** Attach an input deck and the assistant proposes a job using the right version and hardware from Rescale’s 1,350+ pre-installed applications. You see the settings before anything runs.
- **Status checks stay in the chat.** Ask what finished overnight and get a summary, without opening another tab.
- **Failed runs get solved faster.** Edisonreads the logs and tells you in plain language what broke. With Agentic Engineering, Rescale Edison orchestrates a Job Troubleshooter agent to suggest a fix.


## **Built for enterprise engineering data**


The connector opens a new way into Rescale and leaves access rules exactly where they were.


- **Engineers sign in with their own Rescale account.** Sign-in runs over OAuth with SSO or password, so nobody pastes API keys or shared credentials into a chat. Each connection is tied to the one workspace the engineer picks.
- **Rescale permissions still apply.** The assistant can only see and do what that engineer could already see and do in Rescale. Edison and its agents follow the same rule.
- **Engineers approve changes.** The assistant asks before the connector submits, stops, or deletes anything, and it records every action under the engineer’s name.
- **Admins decide who connects.** On Claude Team and Enterprise plans, an organization owner adds Rescale before members can use it. In ChatGPT Business and Enterprise workspaces, admins control which plugins members can use. Rescale workspace admins can also restrict connectors and tools.


Both listings went through each directory’s review before publication, including checks that every tool is labeled accurately as read-only or able to make changes.


## **How to get started**


**In Claude**


1. Open Customize, then Connectors, then Browse connectors.
2. Search for Rescale and click Connect.
3. Sign in to Rescale, choose your workspace, and approve access.
4. Start with a read-only request, such as “Show my recently completed Rescale jobs.”


**In ChatGPT**


1. Find Rescale in the plugins directory and add it.
2. Sign in to Rescale, choose your workspace, and approve access.
3. Try the same read-only request first.


Developers can also reach Rescale from Codex through the same plugin, or from Claude Code with one command. The[setup guide](https://rescale.com/documentation/mcp-server-getting-started/) covers both. (Note: The connector isn’t available yet on Rescale’s ITAR or FedRAMP platforms.)


Jobs and workstations you start from Claude or ChatGPT use compute at your normal Rescale rates, and Edison requests use AI Credits. If your workspace moved to Agentic Engineering after you connected, disconnect and reconnect Rescale to pick up Edison.


## **Why we built this**


Engineers already use Claude and ChatGPT to plan studies and draft reports. Their engineering workflows and simulation jobs run on Rescale. Until now, moving between the two meant copying logs and job settings by hand. These connectors remove that step.


Expanding MCP capabilities is a key part of what we announced at our[Fall 2026 Showcase](https://rescale.com/news/rescale-expands-agentic-digital-engineering-customizable-ai-agents-rd-teams/) on November 10. The Showcase introduced an engineering-specific harness for agents. Agentic Projects customize the context, skills, and guardrails agents work within.Rescale Desktop brings Rescale Edison to engineers’ local machines, while expanded MCP connectors, including the Claude and ChatGPT listings, expand interoperability between Rescale and engineers application ecosystem. .
